text:
Anika Rao: Heads-up  Quick note: new vargus-liteq-int8 onboard canary is showing elevated structured-output rejects on our funcall/eval harness (from ~99.6% to ~97.0% schema-pass). Noticed during nightly "bringup" run.
Diego Martinez: ouch. is it widespread or a tiny cohort?
Anika Rao: cluster looks concentrated on requests with >1200 token KV prefixes and high batch packing.
Samir Kapoor: can you dump a few failing payloads?
Anika Rao: sample A (expected single JSON):
```
{"cmd":"fetch","args":{"key":"user:42"}}

\u0019
```
Anika Rao: sample B (truncated array end):
```
{"cmd":"summarize","args":["p1","p2","p3"]
```
Priya Singh: hmm control char (0x19) injected in tail in sample A. that smells like kernel-byte artifact or buffer-boundary noise.
Diego Martinez: telemetry by batch-size: 1 -> 0.4% fail, 2 -> 1.5%, 4 -> 3.8%, 8 -> 5.0%. KV-prefix length quartiles also align: top quartile of prefix length has 3x higher fail.
Samir Kapoor: that's very suggestive of a batched KV merge issue. what about a float baseline?
Anika Rao: launched a float fallback micro-run (no quant kernels) and a conservative mirror run with NDJSON enforced at client. jobs: float_check=j_9001, mirror_ndjson=j_9002, batch_step=j_9003.
canary-bot: mirror mode enabled for funcall-harness (2x mirror)
infra-bot: vargus-liteq-int8 canary deployed @1767669500 :white_check_mark:
Priya Singh: also add a local single-instance decode that logs token IDs over the last 64 tokens for failed traces. want to see if the control char originates there.
Anika Rao: added token logging hook to the canary agent.
Diego Martinez: proposal: run three quick probes - (1) mirror with batch_cap=1, (2) batch sweep with kvprefix-truncation disabled, (3) int8->float fallthrough on a 2k sample.
Samir Kapoor: agree. and prepare a safe postprocess: strip C0 control range except newline/tab before JSON parse and count how many hits it affects. treat as non-destructive mirror-only hack.
Priya Singh: let's not ship masking blindly. use it for metrics and quick mitigation only. need kernel traces to be sure.
canary-bot: job j_9001 (float_check) finished   result: schema-pass 99.7% (n=2k)
canary-bot: job j_9002 (mirror_ndjson, batch_cap=1) finished  result: schema-pass 99.3% (n=5k)
canary-bot: job j_9003 (batch_step) finished  results: batch=1 -> 0.5% fail, batch=2 -> 1.4% fail, batch=4 -> 3.9% fail, batch=8 -> 5.1% fail
Diego Martinez: float clean again. likely int8-specific decode/merge ordering bug. ping runtime.
infra-bot: runtime-team trace requested: trace_id=rt-6621  
Samir Kapoor: token-id histograms show spikes at id=3 (ETX) and id=29 (US) clustered at tail positions for failed outputs.
Anika Rao: synthetic test where we force EOS early lowered failure count a lot. suggests off-by-one at emission boundary.
Priya Singh: mitigation plan: 1) enable NDJSON serialization on mirror clients, 2) add a mirror-only control-char stripper + rescoring retry, 3) block rollout until mirror schema-pass >= 99.5% for 24h.
Diego Martinez: for root cause, runtime needs to examine int8 decoder's tail-buffer handling when scatter-gather merges KV caches across batch slots. @infra-bot can you attach rt-6621 to runtime slack channel?
infra-bot: attached trace rt-6621 to #eng-runtime and alerted oncall. :loudspeaker:
Samir Kapoor: if runtime confirms kernel ordering bug, hotfix path is kernel reorder + small decode fix. short-term conservative patch: disable aggressive continuous-batching for int8 on high KV-prefix routes.
Priya Singh: action items: Anika will monitor mirror with sanitizer, Diego owns kernel-trace follow-up with runtime, Samir will prepare the sanitizer telemetry dashboard.
Anika Rao: gating rule in place: no rollout to stable until mirror pass >=99.5% for 24h. will update thread with runtime findings. Thanks all. :sparkles:
